summary: This article explains how the Empty Quarter, the world's largest sand desert, was shaped by wind and climate, and how animals and people have survived there.
introduce: Read the title “The Empty Quarter: A Sea of Sand” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: everything you can see when you look across an area of land
the line far away where the land or sea seems to meet the sky
to stay alive, especially in a hard place or situation

challengeTerms.def: having very little rain and very dry land
the change of water from a liquid into a gas, usually because of heat
a substance formed when a chemical element joins with oxygen

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that the Empty Quarter is too harsh to be worth exploring? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how animals and people have managed to survive in the Empty Quarter.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review landscape, horizon, and survive, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use arid, evaporation, and oxide in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
